source_quote: Chairperson: Serene Srouji
answer: The Design Department chairperson is Associate Professor Serene Srouji; Assistant Professors are Noura Sammoura and Nadine Zahreddine.

source_quote: The Design Department at Rafik Hariri University strives to be the leader in high-
answer: The Design Department aims to lead progressive design education in Lebanon and the region, developing creative, skilled professionals who solve visual problems, with faculty, students and alumni as trendsetters in design.

source_quote: The Department of Design offers one program leading to a Bachelor of Science degree
answer: The Design Department offers one program leading to a Bachelor of Science in Graphic Design and a minor in Graphic Design.

source_quote: Our mission is to educate students to become successful thinkers and creative designers
answer: The Graphic Design program educates thinkers and creative designers through progressive curricula, social and ethical responsibility, exhibitions, outside juries and workshops, and industry links; it offers print and multimedia courses, VR/AR/3D printing skills, and portfolio and CV development.

source_quote: Effectively communicate messages by juxtaposing images and type to a
answer: Graphic Design graduates will communicate messages with image and type, apply design terminology and process from concept to completion, show technical skills and design thinking, develop marketing and communication solutions, consider social and ethical issues, and prepare a resume, business card and portfolio for job search.

source_quote: including TV stations, advertising agencies, design and packaging firms, editorial firms
answer: Graphic Design graduates work at TV stations, advertising, design, packaging, branding and editorial firms, interactive/web design firms, 3D animation and gaming studios, photography studios, printing presses and publishing houses, as in-house designers at NGOs and banks, or as freelancers; it also leads to product management, marketing and social media roles.

source_quote: The Bachelor of Science in Graphic Design encompasses 111 credit hours spread over
answer: The BS in Graphic Design is 111 credit hours over six semesters and three summer sessions, with the last summer dedicated to Co-op.

source_quote: credit hours of Fine Arts requirement courses listed in the table below. These courses
answer: Graphic Design students take 18 credits of Fine Arts requirements: FADR 200 Drawing I, FADR 202 Drawing II (prereq FADR 200), FADR 210 Rendering and Perspective Techniques, FADR 215 History of Art, FADR 220 Fundamentals of 2D, and FADR 222 Fundamentals of 3D (prereq FADR 220).

source_quote: The business requirement is a three-credit course listed in the table below.
answer: The Graphic Design business requirement is one 3-credit course: BMKA 200 Introduction to Marketing (co-requisite ENGL 210).

source_quote: The set of mandatory graphic design courses encompasses the 51 credits listed in the
answer: The 51 credits of mandatory Graphic Design courses: GRDS 203, 205, 222, 230, 300, 305, 306, 310, 311, 345, 399 (Co-op, 1 cr), 409, 411, 412, 423, 424, 450, and 452 Digital Illustration (2 cr).

source_quote: Students must take 6 credit hours of major elective courses to deepen their knowledge
answer: Graphic Design students take 6 credits of major electives: GRDS 320 UI/UX Design (GRDS 220), 330 Photography II (GRDS 230), 331 Digital Processing (GRDS 222), 350 3D Printing & Prototyping (GRDS 222), 355 Calligraphy (GRDS 305), 375 3D Animation (GRDS 423), 385 VR Illustration and Sculpting (GRDS 300), 381 Book Binding (Junior Standing), 402 Silkscreen (GRDS 300), 403 Painting (FADR 202), 436 Game Design (GRDS 220), 498 Special Topics.

source_quote: Students must take three extra-credit hours in social science/culture to fulfill the five
answer: Graphic Design students must take three extra credit hours in social science/culture to complete the five humanities and social sciences courses required for accreditation.

source_quote: op training, the program is mandated to stipulate additional conditions.
answer: Graphic Design students complete 8 weeks of practical training, usually in the summer of the third year, followed by a faculty member, and submit a formal report, poster and presentation; prerequisites are ENGL 217 and Senior Standing, with possible additional program conditions.

answer: Graphic Design Year 1 Semester 1 (15 credits): ENGL 210, GRDS 220 Introduction to Digital Media, FADR 200 Drawing I, FADR 215 History of Art, FADR 220 Fundamentals of 2D.

source_quote: FADR 222 Fundamentals of 3D 3 FADR 220
answer: Graphic Design Year 1 Semester 2 (15 credits): GRDS 205 Type I, GRDS 222 Advanced Digital Media, FADR 202 Drawing II, FADR 210 Rendering and Perspective Techniques, FADR 222 Fundamentals of 3D.

source_quote: Summer Session (9 credits)
answer: Graphic Design first summer (9 credits): ARAB 212, GRDS 203 Introduction to Graphic Design, GRDS 230 Photography I, and a 1-credit Community & Sustainability course.

source_quote: Year 2, Semester 1 (18 Credits)
answer: Graphic Design Year 2 Semester 1 (18 credits): BMKA 200, ENGL 217, GRDS 300 Illustration, GRDS 305 Type II, GRDS 310 Design I, and Social Sciences/Culture Elective I.

source_quote: Year 2, Semester 2 (15 Credits)
answer: Graphic Design Year 2 Semester 2 (15 credits): GRDS 306 Type III, GRDS 311 Design II, GRDS 423 Motion Graphics, GRDS 335 Production, GRDS 345 History of Graphic Design. Second summer (9 credits): GRDS 360, Social Sciences/Culture Elective II, and a Humanities/Fine Arts Elective.

source_quote: Year 3, Semester 1 (15 Credits)
answer: Graphic Design Year 3 Semester 1 (15 credits): GRDS 409 Design Writing Research, GRDS 411 Design III, GRDS 424 Web and Interactive Design, GRDS 440 Design & Social Impact, and Major Elective I.

source_quote: Year 3, Semester 2 (14 Credits)
answer: Graphic Design Year 3 Semester 2 (14 credits): GRDS 412 Design IV, GRDS 452 Digital Illustration, GRDS 450 Branding & Advertising, Social Sciences/Culture Elective III, Major Elective II; final summer (1 credit): GRDS 399 Co-op.

source_quote: This course is a comprehensive introduction to the art of drawing. Students learn how
answer: FADR 200 Drawing I, 3(2,2): introduction to drawing objects, planes and volumes accurately using lines, shades, tones and wet/dry media, with composition and perspective basics.

source_quote: This drawing course teaches students the basics of drawing the human figure through
answer: FADR 202 Drawing II, 3(2,2): drawing the human figure through anatomy and proportion, figure in space, media exploration and developing a personal style. Prerequisite: FADR 200.

source_quote: This course introduces students to perspective techniques in rendering three-
answer: FADR 210 Rendering and Perspective Techniques, 3(2,2): perspective techniques for rendering 3-D objects and scenes on 2-D surfaces, composition, conceptualization and light rendering.

source_quote: This course focuses on the student's visual awareness by introducing the fundamentals
answer: FADR 220 Fundamentals of 2D, 3(2,2): 2-D design elements (line, texture, pattern, tone, form, color, light, balance, proportion), design principles, composition and color theory.

source_quote: This course extends two-dimensional design concepts into volumetric relationships,
answer: FADR 222 Fundamentals of 3D, 3(2,2): volumetric design with paper, cardboard, wood, wire, metal and plaster, exploring modularity, relief, structure, symmetry, space and mass. Prerequisite: FADR 220.

source_quote: Graphic design is a creative process that combines art and technology to communicate
answer: GRDS 203 Introduction to Graphic Design, 3(3,0): elements, principles and process of graphic design from topic choice to final presentation, with practical visual communication exercises. Prerequisite: GRDS 205.

source_quote: Type, characters, and letterforms are the essential building blocks of visual
answer: GRDS 205 Type I, 3(3,0): anatomy of type, type terminology, history of type classification and standardization, and the difference between calligraphy and typography.

answer: The course description lists GRDS 220 as the prerequisite for GRDS 205 Type I.
